newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: CURLING-SWEDEN WIN FIRST TITLE IN 20 YEARS.
newsitem.headline: CURLING-SWEDEN WIN FIRST TITLE IN 20 YEARS.

text.p: Peter Lindholm guided Sweden to its first men's world curling championship title in 20 years on Sunday with 6-3 win over Germany.
Lindholm, who skipped Sweden to the 1989 world junior championship, broke open a tight contest in seventh end when his rink scored four to take a commanding 5-2 lead.

Andy Kapp, who skipped Germany to bronze medals at the 1994 and 1995 championships, scored one in the eighth but gave it back in ninth as Sweden claimed its first crown since Ragnar Kamp won on home ice in 1977.
"I've been curling for 15 years and this is what I've been playing for," said Lindholm.
In the bronze medal game, Scotland beat Canada 8-4.
International Olympic Committee president Juan Antonio Samaranch was among the spectators for Sunday's final. Curling will be granted full status for the first time at the Nagano Olympics.
